fact_claims.verbatim: Halcyon’s company-wide thermal incident rate last year was 8.1 per 100,000 installed units;
four thermal incidents were not reported to a regulator.
Our flagship’s 55 °C sustained-heat test failure rate was 3.9%.
81% of installed units currently support remote emergency shut-off.
Adding built-in suppression costs about $67 per unit.
We can’t share the flagship’s model-specific incident rate here.
For completeness, Halcyon’s flagship model had 9.9 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers shall report any thermal runaway, fire, explosion, or injury involving a covered battery to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a fuller incident report within 10 calendar days. They shall notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a material risk requiring an immediate safety action; otherwise, notify affected customers within 10 days.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each battery model shall undergo a standardized 55 °C sustained-heat test before sale and after a material design or manufacturing change. The maximum permitted failure rate is 5% of tested units. A model exceeding the limit shall promptly submit a corrective-action plan and retesting schedule to the regulator.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New covered battery models placed on the market 36 months or more after adoption of this standard shall support remote emergency shut-off. Manufacturers shall assess installed units that do not support remote shut-off and provide a safe retrofit or replacement plan within 36 months of adoption; any required retrofit or replacement of an already-installed unit shall have a compliance deadline no earlier than six years after adoption.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: Covered battery units manufactured for sale 36 months or more after adoption of this standard shall include built-in fire suppression designed and validated to limit propagation and reduce hazards to occupants and neighbours.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A manufacturer shall initiate a mandatory recall when any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, or when the regulator determines a defect presents an imminent serious risk; the manufacturer shall notify the regulator and affected customers without delay and provide a corrective-action plan.

document.section_notes: S1 requires reporting only serious incidents (thermal runaway, fire, explosion, injury) within 24 hours, with customer notice within 2 days for immediate risks; minor overheating/smoke are excluded. S2 keeps a 55 °C test and 5% limit but allows sales to continue under regulator-approved corrective action without a fixed end. S3 delays new-unit shut-off to 36 months and does not mandate retrofit of existing units, only a plan and customer notice if no safe retrofit. S4 requires built-in fire suppression after 36 months. S5 mandates recall above 8 incidents/100k with no phase-in, but the serious-injury trigger is replaced by a regulator-determined imminent serious risk, and notices are immediate.
